title: Tips for Noobs, Skills, Enemies, etc. (looking for balance)

posts.author: cebmetal
posts.body:
The examples provided in the MZ are very basic, in terms of enemies, skills and items.
Although I'm making a game a bit more focused on narrative, graphic adventure, to make good use of it I need a minimum of rpg!
The problem is that I'm afraid that either I'll make it insufferably difficult, or too easy and at the end instead of challenge it will be something that is "annoying".
For MV I know that someone had made the data base of the ACE, if I remember correctly for the new version.
But, if you have to do it manually, some tips on how to manage it.
The enemies raise their life and attack +5, and so they are creating?
I'm at zero with that!
Thank you!

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
I like to think of something I call the "default class". Just an average joe schmoe stats wise, just to get some base values.
Then you go and adjust the stats to be more focused on something. Warrior? More HP, DEF, ATK. Lower MDEF, AGI, LUCK, MP, MAT.
Mage? More MAT, MP, AGI. Less HP, LUCK, you get the idea.
Then I'd like to go and make some beginner gear that's just gonna boost the stats a little bit, just so the heros don't start naked.
Then with those values, go and make some enemies for the player to fight with that setup.
Figure out the stats for those enemies. How? By playtesting. Shouldn't be hard to kill some beginner enemies, but they shouldn't just be cardboard either because what's the point of giving those enemies unique skills, if they can't survive a single hit?
From there it's just gonna be and increase of existing values more or less.
playtest against a party with the gear they're approximately going to have at the point in the game they would face these enemies. Rinse and repeat.

Hello there ! It really depends what you intend to have for your game.
For exemple, mine is focusing on low numbers to make strong characters appear ... Well, strong (The main character start with around 33 hp at lvl 1 if i remember correctly in my game).
And the objective is to have something that could be realistic, especially in a D&D faschion. You wont have to use an end-game spell just to kill a bat (I've seen in a lot of RPG Maker games, which is completly dumb. Two endgame frost spells + one ultimate of one of the main characters, to kill a random encounter bat, WHILE THE WHOLE PARTY IS OVERLEVELED ... Just ... No. Please ...)
Problem with low numbers is that you have to do the perfect balance for damage render (In my case, DMG from basic attack is 1 time the ATK of the character + the bonus ATK from the weapon).
For defense, 1 point = 1 point of damage mitigated (Objective in the end will have to get something like the Pokemon damage calculation formula since the stats will be kinda close in some regards).
Only thing that need to be done to have this kind of thing work tho : Prevent 0 damages from occuring, or create a % damage reduction formula. (Well, one or the other, i'll work on that later).
=> Since the starting stats are so low, 10 atk into 11 defense will deal zero damage, but with higher numbers, it'll work fine since the stat disparity will become greater.
But you need to have a clear idea of what kind of balance you want : realistic or pure fantasy. In my game, you wont feel good after taking a meteor spell from a renowned Red Dragon.

For now, i'm searching for ways to prevent 0 damages from happening. So i tryed to add % health damage to every damage calculations, but hmm ... It works, but at the same time, it doesn't prevent 0 damage from happening still.
Balancing early game is the hardest, maybe i'll have to creatt two sets of formulas, one for early, one for late game.
The % health damage works very well with higher levels it seems like, but will still permit strong ennemies to be shown as strong. While still taking little damage from weak attacks, like it should be in real life.
Even if you have plate gauntlets for your hands, you take a hit with a sword, your fingers wont be cut, but the impact, oh damn. You're gonna feel it (There are videos of crazy dudes testing armors and protections just to see if it works, and damn. Sometimes. It does hurts. A lot. You're not injured, but it stings very much).
You take a spear thrust in the gut while wearing chainmail, you're still gonna feel pain from the impact, the injury will probably be non existant, or very minor, but still an injury nonetheless. Every beast can be put down if you accumulate enough minor injuries on it, its gonna get tired, and finally die (That's the goal for my damage formulas and the game in general).
"Don't get cocky just because you're a big ass dragon. If you get chiped enough, you're gonna die no matter what
"
